Amherst.metaTitle: Wildlife Removal in Amherst, MA | College Town Wildlife Pros
Amherst.metaDescription: Bat, squirrel, and raccoon removal in Amherst, MA. UMass-area rentals, historic village homes, and same-day service — call our local crew.
Amherst.housing_era: Amherst combines a historic town center and UMass Amherst campus with 1800s village homes, faculty colonials, student rentals, and apartment complexes, plus farmhouses in North and South Amherst. Rentals and multi-unit buildings are where wildlife most often goes unnoticed longest.
Amherst.geographic_features: Mount Norwottuck and the Holyoke Range (forested ridge along the southern border), Lawrence Swamp (large wetland in the southern part of town), Fort River (stream corridor through town), Puffer's Pond (pond and woodland in North Amherst)
neighborhoods: Downtown Amherst (historic homes and rentals near the common)

Amherst.wildlife_intro:
Amherst is a busy college town under the Holyoke Range, and its mix of rentals, old village homes, and farmland produces varied wildlife work. Bats are a top call in the historic homes and older apartment buildings, raccoons and gray squirrels fill attics across the neighborhoods, and mice move into rentals every fall. Skunks, opossums, and woodchucks cover the yards in North and South Amherst, and beavers work the Fort River and Lawrence Swamp edges, sometimes flooding trails and low yards.

Rental turnover is the recurring theme — problems found in September often started months earlier. Our crew inspects attics, rooflines, and foundations, removes animals on site under Massachusetts law, and seals entry points so the next tenants inherit a closed house, not a colony. Bat evictions follow the state's May and August-to-mid-October windows and are exclusion-only. Call us and a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent will document what we find for you or your landlord.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost here?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the species, how the animal got in, and how much exclusion and cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts. Simple one-animal jobs cost less than bat exclusion or attic cleanup after a long stay. Call us for an assessment of your home.

faqs.q: Our Amherst rental had mice and scratching all winter — where do we start?
faqs.a: Start with a full inspection: in Amherst rentals, mice usually enter at foundation and utility gaps while squirrels use the roofline, and the two need different sealing. Our crew identifies each entry, removes animals on site, and seals with chew-proof materials. Call us in the fall before cold weather drives the full winter push indoors.

Northampton.wildlife_intro:

Raccoons and gray squirrels are the everyday attic intruders, bats roost in the Victorian-era homes and downtown buildings, and skunks and opossums work the porches and gardens citywide. Woodchucks favor the sunny lots toward the Oxbow farmland, rats appear near the older commercial basements, and beavers along the Mill River can flood low properties.

Most Northampton jobs are won or lost on the inspection: Victorian rooflines hide several entries, and sealing only the active hole just moves the problem. Our crew maps the whole structure, removes animals on site under Massachusetts law, and seals every gap. The southern Connecticut River valley is also copperhead range — that endangered snake is safety and referral only. For the rest, call us and a licensed Problem Animal Control agent will handle it promptly.

Our crew treats South Hadley homes as whole systems — roofline, chimney, foundation, and outbuildings — removes animals on site under Massachusetts law, and seals the entries. Everything else, from a squirrel in the soffit to a raccoon family in the chimney, is work our licensed Problem Animal Control crew handles daily. Call us to get started.

Easthampton.wildlife_intro:
Easthampton sits on the Manhan River under the Mount Tom range, and its mill-era housing takes wildlife pressure from the river, the pond, and the ridge all at once. Raccoons and gray squirrels lead the calls in the older homes and multifamily buildings, bats roost in attics throughout the city, and skunks and opossums are common under porches and in gardens. Rats follow the old mill and commercial basements, woodchucks work the open lots, and beavers on the Manhan can back water into low yards.

In the multifamily stock, our crew inspects connected rooflines as one system, removes animals on site under Massachusetts law, and seals every entry point — partial work just moves the noise to the next unit over. Mount Tom is timber rattlesnake habitat, and that state-Endangered species is safety and referral only. For all other calls, a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent from our crew will inspect, explain, and do the work. Call us when something moves in.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost here?

faqs.q: Are the snakes around Mount Tom in Easthampton dangerous?

Never approach a snake you cannot identify. Our crew can identify from a photo taken at a safe distance and will refer rattlesnake sightings to MassWildlife — they are never a removal job.

Belchertown.wildlife_intro:
Belchertown borders the Quabbin Reservoir's protected watershed, one of the largest undeveloped areas in Massachusetts, so its farms and lake houses sit next to serious wildlife habitat. Raccoons and gray squirrels are the routine attic calls, bats roost in farmhouses, barns, and lake cottages, and skunks, opossums, and woodchucks cover the fields and gardens. Beavers are a standing issue on Jabish Brook and the town's wetlands, flooding driveways and septic systems, and mice fill seasonal cottages over the winter.

Distance from neighbors means problems here can grow quietly — a bat colony in a cottage or raccoons in a barn may go a full season unnoticed. Our crew inspects house and outbuildings together, removes animals on site as Massachusetts law requires, and seals what can be sealed. Beaver flooding is handled through the proper permit route, which we explain up front. Call us and a MassWildlife-licensed Problem Animal Control agent will assess the whole property, not just the noisy corner.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost here?
faqs.a: Cost depends on the species, how the animal got in, and how much exclusion and cleanup the home needs, so our crew inspects first and explains the options before any work starts. Simple one-animal jobs cost less than bat exclusion or attic cleanup after a long stay. Call us for an assessment of your home.

faqs.q: Beavers are flooding our Belchertown lot — is trapping the only answer?
faqs.a: Not always. A licensed Problem Animal Control agent can trap beavers in season, and off-season work generally needs a Board of Health emergency permit; in some settings a flow device keeps water at a safe level while the beavers stay. Our crew will look at your site and recommend the lawful option that actually protects the property.
